about: Each State GIS ahupuaʻa unit (boundaries/ahupuaa.geojson, joined by gisId) and its class after the Māhele of 1848: crown (the lands Kamehameha III reserved to himself), government (the lands he gave to the government, with those the chiefs later surrendered in lieu of commutation), konohiki (lands awarded to a chief or konohiki, with the awardee as the record writes the name), mixed (more than one class recorded within the unit) or unknown (no source read records it). A class is taken only from a record of that land, never from its name. Kuleana, the house lots and farms the Land Commission awarded to the people who worked the land, lie inside these classes and are not a class of their own here.
method: Three records are joined. (1) OHA Kīpuka, Ahupuaa_State: a historic land type per ahupuaʻa (Crown Land 1848, Government Land 1848, Surrendered in lieu of Commutation), joined to the State units by area (716 of 727 names agree; a State unit takes an OHA record only where the names agree). (2) OHA Kīpuka, Crown_Lands_State: tenure polygons with Buke Māhele page numbers and, for konohiki lands, the chief the king relinquished each to. It maps every land of Kauaʻi, Molokaʻi, Lānaʻi and Niʻihau and the Crown lands elsewhere; on those four islands it decides, with shares by area. (3) The 1929 Indices of Awards: the awards its index by awardee and its index by land mark "Ahp", an award of the whole ahupuaʻa, matched by name within the island and district of the page; on Hawaiʻi, Maui and Oʻahu these are the konohiki record, and on the four islands Kīpuka maps they agree with it in 52 of 53 cases. Where an award of the whole land meets a bare listing of it as government land, the award stands and the listing is kept under disputed; Kīpuka notes that the Buke Māhele itself lists some awarded lands on its government pages by mistake. The Act of 7 June 1848, as the Indices reprint it, lists the Crown and Government lands by name: it carries 57 of the 70 crown listings and 182 of the 264 government listings checked against it (the rest are lost in its scan or absent from it), and its ʻili are given as parts of the lands they lie in. Shares are fractions of the unit's area, null where a class is recorded and its extent is not.

precision.whole: the class is recorded for this ahupuaʻa as a whole
precision.combined: the State unit joins several ahupuaʻa and the class is recorded for them
precision.part: the class is recorded for part of the unit only (a share, an ʻili, a part of an award)

fields: gisId, name and islandId as in boundaries/ahupuaa.geojson; class; precision; awardee (konohiki: a name or a list); parts [{ class, share (0–1 or null), awardee?, ili? (the number of ʻili of that class the 1848 Act lists inside), how? }]; how (how a land came to its class); later [{ class, year, how }] (a status given after the Māhele, such as the unassigned lands declared Crown Land in 1890); disputed [{ class, source }] (a class another source gives the same land); note; sources (ids in sources.json); refs (Buke Māhele pages, award numbers, Indices leaves).
